RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 30

Pointing out that the panel was all women will likely be perceived as an unsubstantiated accusation and damage your professional reputation. An all-female panel alone does not indicate bias; selection committees are typically assembled based on administrative roles or availability.

While your formal leadership credentials appear stronger on paper, final decisions often hinge on interview performance, stakeholder alignment, references, and institutional vision. Furthermore, a two-week delay in receiving formal feedback is standard bureaucracy in educational administration.

Do not bring up the panel's gender composition. Instead, send a polite follow-up requesting the written explanation. If you decide to challenge the outcome, base your case strictly on documented qualifications, scoring rubrics, and procedural fairness.
